glossary.definition: SWQT test case specification workbook FMWIFSM036A01 — the SWE1_BT deliverable; header row 9, data row 10, Spec Reference = column 14
Software Requirements Analysis — source of the bilingual When/And/Case/Then AC blocks; treated as a generic wrapper when it conflicts with CFTS
Customer Functional Test Specification — the authoritative clause source for TC content (wins over SWRA AC on conflict, §10.1)
System Architectural Design docx — source of the full long SYS3 Spec Reference form for SWEs without CFTS coverage
Escalation channel to the requirements author for unresolvable conflicts, dead-code gaps, and SWRA↔CFTS mismatches; recorded in remarks, tracked across sessions
Bluetooth Streaming Audio source (CFTS025); source selection observed on CAN as STATUS_TELEMATIC.CurrentSource = 23 and HFM_BlueTooth_1_Selected
Engineering mode display (CFTS011); entered via press-and-hold top-left + bottom-right corners for 5 seconds
com.test.btapp (app-system-debug.apk, md5 a3eff9310c9fb773417a50f603c0e8a4), system-signed with BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED; the standard HU-side test harness
max_granularity split mode: one verification point per TC, applied uniformly to the whole batch once chosen (connect/disconnect states and all mode variants separate)

feature_model.normal: Adapter enable/disable via adb shell svc bluetooth enable|disable; reconnect verified with logcat and dumpsys bluetooth_manager
feature_model.abnormal: Async connect followed immediately by a state query races — an explicit wait step with APK broadcast confirmation is mandatory before any state query
feature_model.boundary: Adapter disable is the standard fault-injection point for connection tests, but INVALID for call-state tests (see interactions)

feature_model.normal: Call control via test-APK PhoneFragment; steps use real APK labels such as hfpClient.disconnect(device)
feature_model.abnormal: getHfpDevice() returning null causes silent return-void in all call-control methods
feature_model.boundary: SWE1_BT_070 is the only TC allowed to use HU adapter disable in a call-state context (targets proxy-not-ready itself)

feature_model.normal: Contact/call-log sync exercised via PBAP connect/disconnect in ContactsFragment
feature_model.abnormal: deleteData / downloadContacts / downloadCallLog buttons are permanently dead code — never referenced in steps; workaround is PBAP connect/disconnect plus a remarks note

feature_model.normal: Playback control via MusicFragment; control→command→display triad for one user action is ONE TC (§7.7)
feature_model.abnormal: Repeat softkey/icon shows Unavailable state on BTSA Source screens when the source does not support Repeat (CFTS025 §3.1.1.4.3.7)
feature_model.boundary: Repeat All / Repeat One / Shuffle are separate TCs under max_granularity split mode

feature_model.normal: Selecting BT audio source updates CAN: STATUS_TELEMATIC.CurrentSource = 23, HFM_BlueTooth_1_Selected
feature_model.boundary: CAN reads use the wording: Read the <Signal> value on CAN and record as <Var>_initial/_after

feature_model.normal: BT information page verified one verification point per TC; connect-state and disconnect-state are separate TCs
SPP link tested with Serial Bluetooth Terminal (Kai Morich), UUID 00001101 (BT_121/122, BT_131/132)

interactions.rule: HU adapter disable makes getHfpDevice() return null → call-control methods silently no-op. Adapter disable is an INVALID injection point for call-state tests; sole exception SWE1_BT_070 (proxy-not-ready).
BTSA playback TCs that assert source selection must observe the CAN signals (CurrentSource = 23, HFM_BlueTooth_1_Selected), not only the HMI.
Every async connect/disconnect call is followed by an explicit wait step confirmed via the APK broadcast listener before any state query (known systematic timing race).
Phonebook/call-log data operations route through PBAP connect/disconnect because the APK's data buttons are dead code; each such workaround carries a remarks note.
